terms.comment: Classically the Greek word for an image, which Pliny uses once (Lewis & Short).

icon.against: Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked: īcon, ŏnis
icon.html: Greek εἰκών, with omega in the nominative and omicron in the other cases (εἰκόνος), whence the short o of īconis. Traupman 261 prints īcōn, īconis.

sources: Lewis & Short: icon
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 261, 331.
